A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 18-page versions of the same PRO-SCALE paper. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original PRO-SCALE experiments on COCO and Cityscapes, additional task evaluations, and component analyses in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, task evaluations and appendix analyses, including the segmentation accuracy and computational-cost results in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: The progressive token expansion, Light-Pixel Embedding module, token recalibration, decoder and losses are unchanged. Section 3.1 only shortens the wording introducing the encoder structure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain COCO and Cityscapes segmentation, COCO detection and joint-task evaluations, and open-vocabulary segmentation with ADE20K cross-evaluation. The ImageNet pretraining coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments, including M2F, Lite-M2F, RT-M2F, MaskFormer, PEM, YOSO, RAP-SAM and ReMaX. The detection, MaskDINO and open-vocabulary comparisons are also retained.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same splits, metrics, image sizes, backbone configurations and training budgets. The additional task evaluations and the 100-image token-redundancy analysis use the same reported protocols.

E4.justification: The component, LPE, encoder-depth, backbone and pretraining analyses are unchanged. Appendices B–C retain the same pooling comparison, token-redundancy analysis, TRC ablations, temperature sensitivity, speed comparisons and qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The existing descriptions of average GFLOPs and image-averaged token similarity are unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 reports SWIN-T PRO-SCALE (3,3,3) at 52.82 PQ, 171.70 total GFLOPs and 56.18 encoder GFLOPs in both versions.

T1.justification: The token-sequence definitions in Equations 1–3 and the TRC expression in Equation 4 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, propositions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and efficiency claims, including approximately 52% encoder and 27% overall GFLOPs reduction on COCO with preserved performance. Claims about applicability beyond universal segmentation are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations concerning token redundancy, local-detail preservation, LPE efficiency and TRC benefits remain the same. The performance-efficiency interpretations and applicability qualifications are unchanged, with no new substantive limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same software, optimizer, hyperparameters, losses and eight-A6000-GPU training disclosure. The repository URL and its hyperlink target are unchanged; adding 'Code available here:' introduces no new access information.

R1.justification: Section 2 retains the same positioning relative to universal segmentation, efficient DETR encoders and task-specific panoptic methods. The bibliography is identical after accounting for entries flowing between pages.

P1.justification: v3 updates affiliations, adds a work-attribution footnote, corrects the corresponding-author email and labels the existing code link. It also briefly tightens the encoder-structure wording in Section 3.1; the narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded affiliation block and small spacing adjustments cause limited page reflow. The conclusion now fits on page 10 instead of continuing onto page 11. Figures and tables retain their content and structure, and the appendix pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: v3 updates administrative information and makes small wording and layout refinements, including keeping the conclusion together. The method, evidence, reproducibility details and appendix analyses remain unchanged, so these editorial adjustments do not meaningfully alter overall paper quality.
